title: Microrelease guardchain and ops heuristics (working notes)
content:
Context: quick-working sketch for a lightweight, cross-functional microrelease guardchain that lets product teams push small LLM-driven changes (model variant, prompt tweak, reranker adjustment) while bounding risk across quality, latency, and cost. This is intentionally more prescriptive than the big playbooks — operational heuristics we can teach stewards and embed in automation.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Push 0.1%–5% traffic increments safely for experiments and small feature rollouts.
- Detect quality regressions quickly on small cohorts and automatically contain/expose traffic when thresholds trip.
- Keep ops overhead low: runbook + 1-2 automated guard rails = most rollouts.
- Integrate cost awareness so rollouts that degrade unit economics auto-quarantine.

Core concepts (quick defs):
- Microrelease: any change with <5% initial exposure, intended to iterate quickly.
- Guardchain: a series of short-circuit checks (signal quorum) evaluated in order — if any fails the chain, traffic is reduced or diverted.
- Steward: named human owner for a microrelease who gets paging on soft failures and must own remediations.
- Signal quorum: require N distinct signal groups (quality, latency, cost, infra errors) before an automated reversion.

Proposed guardchain (priority order):
1) Platform health gate (100% synthetic): basic availability and error-rate sweep across regions; failure -> immediate stop. Threshold: 5xx > 0.5% over 1m.
2) Latency shock gate: p50/p95 delta vs baseline model. Immediate soft-hold if p95 increases > 30% and absolute p95 > 1200ms.
3) Cost sentinel: per-token cost uplift (estimated) > 15% over historical average for the route -> hold and notify finance owner.
4) Quality triage gate (tiered):
   - Automated evals on a small prompt set (n=200) with golden labels: if F1/utility drops > 6% -> escalate.
   - Crowd-sampled user synth-run (n=500) latency-weighted sampling: if sentiment/accept-rate drops > 8% -> quarantine.
5) Behavioural drift probe: rerank/fail modes (safety triggers + hallucination detection): if hallucination detector rate > 3x baseline -> pause.
6) Oscillation dampener: if traffic toggles more than 2 times in 10 minutes due to cascading checks, hold for human review.

Signal handling logic (heuristics):
- Single-signal vs quorum: avoid flip-flopping on noisy signals. Require 2 of {latency, quality, cost, error-rate} within a 10m sliding window for automated rollback.
- Soft vs hard actions: soft = stop growth (freeze at current slice), hard = immediate rollback to previous stable variant. Soft requires steward ack within 15m, otherwise escalate to hard.
- Reversion path should be atomic and fast: model variant swap + prefix-cache flush + circuit-marking to route to fallback. We must ensure TTLs on caches are respected.

Experiment power and sampling notes (for A/B microreleases):
- For small-signal LLM changes (e.g., subtle prompt tweaks), realistic MDES (min detectable effect size) for accept-rate ~ 3–5% needs ~20k users per arm over 7 days for ~80% power. If that's infeasible, rely on higher-sensitivity signal (evaluation harness) instead of pure product metric.
- Use weighted sampling (by route and persona) to ensure cohorts reflect heavy and light token users. Weight by 7-day token volume quantiles.
- Precompute minimum exposure window: 48 hours AND at least 1,000 unique sessions OR 50k tokens whichever comes later. This prevents early false positives.

Telemetry & dashboards (must-haves):
- Per-cohort stream: p50/p95 latency, per-token cost, 5xx rate, user acceptance (binary), eval-score distribution with small-sample confidence intervals.
- Quick-compare view: current slice vs baseline over rolling 1h / 6h / 24h. Highlight deltas > 10% in red.
- Signal provenance: timestamped list of checks that tripped and the raw stats that caused them.
- Incident link templates: auto-create ticket when hard rollback triggered, include snapshot links, sample requests, and top offending prompts.

Human workflows and escalation:
- Steward roster: every microrelease must list steward (name, Slack handle, phone). Steward receives primary on-call for 1 hour after exposure increase.
- If soft-hold triggered: steward must ack in 15m and decide to continue, rollback, or widen evaluation. Lack of ack -> system auto-rolls back after 30m.
- On hard rollback: Incident owner is the original steward; SRE + model owner looped. Postmortem template required within 72 hours.

Preflight checklist (must pass before any public microrelease):
- Baseline snapshots: last 7 days of metrics for route and model pinned.
- Eval harness run with >= 3 prompt families and automated reference scores.
- Synthetic stress: run 2x normal token concurrency for 10 minutes in canary slice.
- Failure-mode playbook link included in the release description.
- Canary slice defined: % exposure, cohorts, ramp schedule, steward contact.

Ramp plan (example conservative):
- Start: 0.1% for 20m (smoke), evaluate signals for 1h. If green -> 1% for 1h. If green -> 5% for 6h. If green -> 20% over 24h. At any step, failing guardchain -> revert to previous stable.

Open design questions / TODOs (for group):
- How to compute continuous per-token cost uplift when quantization changes the GPU profile (we need an infra-side estimator; ticket RINF-3582).
- Exact thresholds for hallucination detector — need labeling study (Priya to own).
- Should we bake a ML-based meta-guard that learns normal delta ranges per route instead of static thresholds? Pros/cons noted below.
- Alert fatigue: define smarter paging only for stewards and secondary owners; general channel notifications are muted to prevent noise.

Short-run action items (next 2 sprints):
- (Ethan) Implement guardchain orchestration prototype in rollout-orchestrator (PR 78 is the skeleton).
- (Riley) Add microrelease dashboard tiles + signal provenance to devconsole.
- (Priya) Kick off labeling study for hallucination thresholds; propose interim proxy metric.
- (Maya) Draft steward rotation template and add to release template in Confluence.

Notes-to-self / informal:
- Keep the automation readable — ops must be able to reason about 3 actions (grow/freeze/roll back).
- Prefer conservative defaults; teams can opt into aggressive ramps after 3 successful microreleases.
- Document cases where single-signal auto-rollbacks are acceptable (safety-critical categories).

If helpful, we can run a tabletop rehearsal with a fake microrelease (model: reranker-v2, route: search-relevancy) to validate the playbook. Suggest date: 2026-03-24.

End of notes.
